annotations.description:
Optional. Annotations on the node pool. This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations. The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k. Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required), separated by a slash (/). Prefix must be a DNS subdomain. Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics, with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field `effective_annotations` for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations provide metadata for the node pool and do not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

cluster.rationale: This field identifies the parent cluster for the node pool. It controls placement but does not directly grant access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.rationale: The resource name identifies the node pool but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

project.rationale: The project identifies where the resource is created. It affects placement and ownership but does not directly define access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

subnet_id.description: The subnet where the node pool node run.
subnet_id.rationale: The subnet determines network placement for node pool nodes and should be restricted to approved private subnets to avoid exposing nodes on public networks.

version.description: The Kubernetes version to run on this node pool (e.g. `1.19.10-gke.1000`). You can list all supported versions on a given Google Cloud region by calling GetAwsServerConfig.
version.rationale: The Kubernetes version can affect exposure to known vulnerabilities and should be kept within approved supported versions.

autoscaling.description: Autoscaler configuration for this node pool.

autoscaling.max_node_count.description: Maximum number of nodes in the NodePool. Must be >= min_node_count.
autoscaling.max_node_count.rationale: This setting affects capacity, density, availability, or cost, but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, privileged permissions, data residency, or vulnerability posture.

autoscaling.min_node_count.description: Minimum number of nodes in the NodePool. Must be >= 1 and <= max_node_count.
autoscaling.min_node_count.rationale: Minimum node count affects baseline capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.description: The configuration of the node pool.

config.iam_instance_profile.description: The name of the AWS IAM role assigned to nodes in the pool.
config.iam_instance_profile.rationale: The IAM instance profile controls the permissions granted to node pool instances. Unapproved profiles may grant excessive or unauthorised permissions.

config.instance_type.description: Optional. The AWS instance type. When unspecified, it defaults to `m5.large`.
config.instance_type.rationale: The instance type affects capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.labels.description: Optional. The initial labels assigned to nodes of this node pool. An object containing a list of "key": value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
config.labels.rationale: Labels provide metadata for nodes and support workload scheduling but do not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.security_group_ids.description: Optional. The IDs of additional security groups to add to nodes in this pool. The manager will automatically create security groups with minimum rules needed for a functioning cluster.
config.security_group_ids.rationale: Security groups control network access to node pool instances and should be restricted to approved groups.

config.tags.description: Optional. Key/value metadata to assign to each underlying AWS resource. Specify at most 50 pairs containing alphanumerics, spaces, and symbols (.+-=_:@/). Keys can be up to 127 Unicode characters. Values can be up to 255 Unicode characters.
config.tags.rationale: Tags support resource identification, ownership, and cost allocation but do not directly grant access or permissions.

config.autoscaling_metrics_collection.description: Optional. Configuration related to CloudWatch metrics collection on the Auto Scaling group of the node pool. When unspecified, metrics collection is disabled.

config.autoscaling_metrics_collection.gr.description: The frequency at which EC2 Auto Scaling sends aggregated data to AWS CloudWatch. The only valid value is "1Minute".

config.autoscaling_metrics_collection.me.description: The metrics to enable. For a list of valid metrics, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/APIReference/API_EnableMetricsCollection.html. If you specify granularity and don't specify any metrics, all metrics are enabled.

config.config_encryption.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt node pool configuration.

config.config_encryption.kms_key_arn.description: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt node pool configuration.
config.config_encryption.kms_key_arn.rationale: Sets the KMS key used to encrypt node-pool configuration. A policy should require it to be non-empty so configuration is always CMEK-encrypted; it must not pin a specific key, since keys are team/project-specific.

config.proxy_config.description: Proxy configuration for outbound HTTP(S) traffic.

config.proxy_config.secret_arn.description: The ARN of the AWS Secret Manager secret that contains the HTTP(S) proxy configuration.
config.proxy_config.secret_arn.rationale: Identifier pointing at the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds proxy configuration. It is a reference to an externally-managed resource; a generic platform policy cannot constrain which secret without naming a specific ARN, so it is not a useful policy target.

config.proxy_config.secret_version.description: The version string of the AWS Secret Manager secret that contains the HTTP(S) proxy configuration.
config.proxy_config.secret_version.rationale: The secret version selects a version of an approved proxy secret but does not independently grant access or permissions.

config.root_volume.description: Optional. Template for the root volume provisioned for node pool nodes. Volumes will be provisioned in the availability zone assigned to the node pool subnet. When unspecified, it defaults to 32 GiB with the GP2 volume type.

config.root_volume.iops.description: Optional. The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for GP3 volume.
config.root_volume.iops.rationale: IOPS affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.root_volume.kms_key_arn.description: Optional. The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Customer Managed Key (CMK) used to encrypt AWS EBS volumes. If not specified, the default Amazon managed key associated to the AWS region where this cluster runs will be used.
config.root_volume.kms_key_arn.rationale: The KMS key controls encryption for the node pool root EBS volume and should use an approved customer-managed key.

config.root_volume.size_gib.description: Optional. The size of the volume, in GiBs. When unspecified, a default value is provided. See the specific reference in the parent resource.
config.root_volume.size_gib.rationale: Volume size affects capacity and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.root_volume.throughput.description: Optional. The throughput to provision for the volume, in MiB/s. Only valid if the volume type is GP3. If volume type is gp3 and throughput is not specified, the throughput will defaults to 125.
config.root_volume.throughput.rationale: Throughput affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.root_volume.volume_type.description: Optional. Type of the EBS volume. When unspecified, it defaults to GP2 volume. Possible values: VOLUME_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GP2, GP3
config.root_volume.volume_type.rationale: Volume type affects performance and cost but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, or privileged permissions.

config.ssh_config.ec2_key_pair.description: The name of the EC2 key pair used to login into cluster machines.
config.ssh_config.ec2_key_pair.rationale: The EC2 key pair controls SSH access to node pool machines and should be restricted to approved managed keys.

config.taints.description: Optional. The initial taints assigned to nodes of this node pool.

config.taints.effect.description: The taint effect. Possible values: EFFECT_UNSPECIFIED, NO_SCHEDULE, PREFER_NO_SCHEDULE, NO_EXECUTE

kubelet_config.description: The kubelet configuration for the node pool.

kubelet_config.cpu_cfs_quota.description: Whether or not to enable CPU CFS quota. Defaults to true.
kubelet_config.cpu_cfs_quota.rationale: CPU CFS quota affects scheduling fairness but does not directly grant access or permissions.

kubelet_config.cpu_cfs_quota_period.description: Optional. The CPU CFS quota period to use for the node. Defaults to "100ms".
kubelet_config.cpu_cfs_quota_period.rationale: CPU CFS quota period affects scheduling fairness but does not directly grant access or permissions.

kubelet_config.cpu_manager_policy.description: The CpuManagerPolicy to use for the node. Defaults to "none".
kubelet_config.cpu_manager_policy.rationale: CPU manager policy affects scheduling behaviour but does not directly grant access or permissions.

kubelet_config.pod_pids_limit.description: Optional. The maximum number of PIDs in each pod running on the node. The limit scales automatically based on underlying machine size if left unset.
kubelet_config.pod_pids_limit.rationale: Pod PID limit affects process accounting but does not directly grant access or permissions.

management.description: The Management configuration for this node pool.

management.auto_repair.description: Optional. Whether or not the nodes will be automatically repaired.
management.auto_repair.rationale: Auto-repair affects node availability but does not directly grant access or permissions.

max_pods_constraint.description: The constraint on the maximum number of pods that can be run simultaneously on a node in the node pool.

max_pods_constraint.max_pods_per_node.description: The maximum number of pods to schedule on a single node.
max_pods_constraint.max_pods_per_node.rationale: This setting affects capacity, density, availability, or cost, but does not directly control access, encryption, network exposure, privileged permissions, data residency, or vulnerability posture.

update_settings.description: Optional. Update settings control the speed and disruption of the node pool update.

update_settings.surge_settings.max_surge.description: Optional. The maximum number of nodes that can be created beyond the current size of the node pool during the update process.
update_settings.surge_settings.max_surge.rationale: Max surge controls update speed but does not directly grant access or permissions.

update_settings.surge_settings.max_unava.description: Optional. The maximum number of nodes that can be simultaneously unavailable during the update process. A node is considered unavailable if its status is not Ready.
update_settings.surge_settings.max_unava.rationale: Max unavailable controls update disruption but does not directly grant access or permissions.
